correctness.rationale: The arbitrary-horizon 2-voter lemma follows because Pareto efficiency forces each chosen round to realize maximum total approval h_r(N); EJR+ enforces each singleton's level if its active-round count reaches twice that level. For 3 voters at ≤2 rounds, only a pair unanimously coapproving in both rounds can trigger positive FJR+ despite low satisfaction, and EJR+ prohibits its neglect; the whole group is protected by roundwise Pareto efficiency. An explicit three-voter witness was checked against the exact FJR min-over-subsets benchmark and EJR+ common-candidate condition. Standalone finite exhaustive checks independently corroborate bounded cases; none are invoked to prove universal claims.

value.rationale: The natural question is how small an electorate and time horizon can display a strict Pareto-efficient gap between temporal FJR+ and the conjunction of its two antecedent axioms. The new result establishes a universal all-horizon low-population collapse, a sharp first 3-round/3-voter boundary, and a minimum 2-candidate witness, sharpening the previously exhibited five-voter separation in the general model. This resolves a meaningful finite obstruction and isolates the role of equality-trigger (ii), not merely a textbook example.
